title: Penne alla Sorrentina
subtitle: Penne baked with tomato, basil, and melted mozzarella
excerpt: Penne tossed in a quick tomato and basil sauce, then baked with mozzarella until bubbling and golden at the edges. A Neapolitan classic that is both simple and deeply satisfying.
sourceNotes: Neapolitan home cooking tradition. Named after Sorrento, on the Amalfi Coast. One of the most popular baked pasta dishes in southern Italy.

recipe.freezeNotes: Assemble but do not bake. Freeze in the dish, covered. Bake from frozen at 190C for 35 to 40 minutes until bubbling.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 24 hours ahead and refrigerate. Add 10 minutes to the baking time if cooking from cold.

content.text: Penne alla sorrentina is a baked pasta from the Campania coast, built on a simple tomato sauce and finished with mozzarella. It gives crispy, golden edges and a molten centre. Do not overcook the pasta before baking or it will turn soft.
Heat the oven to 200C. Bring a large pot of well-salted water to the boil.
Warm the olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and fry for 1 minute until pale gold.
Add the tinned tomatoes, half the basil, and salt. Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick.
Cook the penne for 2 minutes less than the packet says. The pasta should still be very firm. Drain and toss with the tomato sauce.
Spread half the pasta into a gratin dish. Scatter over half the mozzarella and half the remaining basil.
Add the remaining pasta, then the rest of the mozzarella. Scatter the parmesan over the top.
Bake for 20 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and the edges are golden. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The pasta is mushy after baking.
items.cause: The penne was fully cooked before going into the oven.
items.fix: Cook the pasta 2 to 3 minutes less than the packet specifies. It will finish cooking in the oven.

items.symptom: The mozzarella has released a lot of water into the dish.
items.fix: Tear the mozzarella and leave it on kitchen paper for 15 minutes before using to draw out excess liquid.

items.symptom: The top is brown but the inside is not hot.
items.cause: The oven temperature was too high.
items.fix: Cover loosely with foil and return to the oven at 180C for another 10 minutes.
